tema: Modals of Deduction — Past (Must Have, Can't Have, Might Have)

cast_dialogue.linea: The past leaves footprints, heroes. 'Must have' follows them with certainty, 'can't have' closes doors, and 'might have' keeps the mystery alive.
The cake has disappeared and there are crumbs on the floor. The dog must have eaten it!
It can't have been the dog — he was outside all afternoon. Look at these wet footprints...
It might have been me... I was so hungry! But I can't have eaten the whole cake alone.
Someone must have used the spare key. Well, mis héroes, the thief must have been very happy — it was my best recipe!

banco_oraciones.oracion: The dog must have eaten the cake.
Someone must have used the spare key.
It might have rained last night.
It can't have been the dog — he was outside.
He might not have seen the message.
Who could have opened the window?
Could she have forgotten the meeting?
Did he eat the cake? He must have.
Was it the cat? It can't have been.
Did she call? She might have — I had a missed call.

inicio.definicion_pragmatica: Deductions about the PAST: must have + participle (almost certain it happened), can't have + participle (almost impossible), might/may/could have + participle (possibly). The modal never changes; the participle carries the tense.

filas: The dog must have eaten it.
It can't have been the cat.

ejercicios.pregunta: There are crumbs everywhere. The dog ___ the cake.
He was outside all afternoon, so it ___ him.
I'm not sure, but it ___ rained last night. The ground is wet.

ejercicios.afirmacion: After 'must have' we use the past participle.
For negative past deduction we say 'mustn't have'.

guion: Ben: Abuela Carmen! Your cake has disappeared!
Abuela Carmen: What?! It was on the table an hour ago.
Ben: The dog must have eaten it. Look at the crumbs!
Kenji: It can't have been the dog — he was outside with me all afternoon.
Sofía: Then who...? Wait. There are wet footprints near the window.
Kenji: Someone must have come in through the window.
Abuela Carmen: Or... it might have been me, sleepwalking again. Mystery solved, mis héroes!

reading.texto: The cake had disappeared from the table. 'The dog must have eaten it,' said Ben, pointing at the crumbs. 'It can't have been the dog — he was outside all afternoon,' replied Kenji. Sofía looked guilty: 'It might have been me... I was so hungry.' Everyone laughed. Someone might have saved a piece for Abuela Carmen, but nobody could remember. The mystery was never solved.
